name: Zhu Fenglian
current_role: Reportedly chairman, New Century School (Dongguan) and related Dongguan property companies (per MarketScreener insider profile 'Feng Lian Zhu')
profile: Listed wealth source is New Century Science and Education, a Dongguan, Guangdong private-school and property group. A MarketScreener profile for 'Feng Lian Zhu' lists her as chairman of New Century School / Dongguan New Century School (since 2010) and of Dongguan Jinshun and Jincheng real-estate firms, with a Sun Yat-sen University degree (1985). The link to the rich-list entry is not confirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; little English or Chinese coverage found. Do not confuse with Zhu Fenglian, the Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson (b. 1977, Meizhou) - a different person. MarketScreener source: https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/FENG-LIAN-ZHU-A11DMM/experience/ . Best route is likely via the school group's official channels.

name: Li Yao
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ye Delin) of New Pearl Group (Xinmingzhu), Foshan ceramic tiles maker
profile: Li Yao and her husband Ye Delin control New Pearl Group, a Foshan, Guangdong building-ceramics and tile maker founded in 1993 with production bases in Guangdong, Jiangxi and Chongqing. The couple jointly held about 86.67% of the company directly at end-2022. New Pearl's planned Shenzhen IPO has stalled since 2023.
interesting_fact: New Pearl is often described as a husband-and-wife company: Li Yao and Ye Delin directly held 86.67% of its equity at the end of 2022.
notes: Very private; husband Ye Delin (chairman/CEO, a former Nanzhuang town hydropower station head) is the public face. Approach via the company site. Avoid IPO/dividend controversies.

name: family Hager
current_role: Hager family owns Hager Group (Hager SE), Blieskastel, Germany; Daniel Hager (3rd generation) chairs the Supervisory Board since Dec 2023; Philipp/Peter Hager are shareholders/board members
profile: The Hager family owns Hager Group, a Franco-German maker of electrical installation, energy distribution, cable management and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC) with 3.5bn+ in revenue and 13,000+ staff. Daniel Hager was CEO 2008-2023 and handed operations to Sabine Busse, becoming Supervisory Board chairman.
interesting_fact: Hager Group owns E3/DC, a German home battery-storage maker, putting a 1950s-era electrical-fittings family firm squarely in the energy-transition business; the group runs twin hubs in Blieskastel (Germany) and Obernai (France).
deep_cut_fact: Besides chairing the supervisory board, Daniel Hager heads the Board of Trustees of the Peter und Luise Hager Foundation, the family's charitable foundation.
notes: Forbes lists this as 'Philip & family Hager'. Daniel Hager is the most public family member and has given interviews on Franco-German identity and family business (Tharawat magazine). Energy angle: E3/DC storage and energy-management business. Press contact Markus Goegele (Hager Group).

name: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Carabao Group PCL (SET: CBG), Thailand
profile: Co-founder and chairman of SET-listed Carabao Group, maker of Carabao Dang energy drink. She moved from her family's financial-services business into property with partner Sathien Sathientham, co-owned Tawandang German Brewery, and in 2002 co-launched Carabao with folk-rock singer Aed Carabao. She also has stakes in Tawandang Distillery (rice whisky) and expanded into beer brewing in 2023.
interesting_fact: Carabao was launched in 2002 with Yuenyong 'Aed Carabao' Opakul, frontman of Thailand's famous Carabao band; she was named to Fortune's 2024 Most Powerful Women Asia list.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy drinks she and Sathien ran Tawandang German Brewery, a Bangkok German-style brewpub (she has been on its board since 1998); she studied at Silpakorn University and did graduate study at Thammasat.
notes: Low-profile; partner Sathien Sathientham is the more public face. Carabao is also known globally for football sponsorship (Carabao Cup).

name: John Edson
current_role: Deceased (J. Orin Edson, founder of Bayliner Marine; died 27 Aug 2019 in Seattle, aged 87)
profile: Founder of Bayliner Marine, which he sold to Brunswick in 1986 for $425 million; later owned yacht builder Westport. Died August 27, 2019.
interesting_fact: He bought the 'Bayliner' brand name for $100 and built it into a boat-manufacturing powerhouse sold to Brunswick for $425 million.
notes: Deceased - death reported by ASU (https://news.asu.edu/20190829-arizona-impact-asu-mourns-loss-j-orin-edson-philanthropist-and-entrepreneur) and Boattest (https://boattest.com/view-news/6501_boating-ENTREPRENEUR-ORIN-EDSON-DIES-AT-87). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Vinod Goenka
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Valor Estate Ltd (formerly DB Realty), Mumbai
profile: Kolkata-born, Mumbai-raised developer (b. 1959) who started in real estate in the early 1980s with Conwood Constructions, co-founded the DB Group with Shahid Balwa around 2006, and leads Valor Estate (renamed from DB Realty in 2024). He is known for Mumbai slum and cluster redevelopment and JVs with Godrej Properties and Lodha.
interesting_fact: In 1994 he diversified into dairy, partnering with US-based Schreiber Foods to set up a dairy plant in Baramati, Maharashtra.
deep_cut_fact: He was a competitive track-and-field athlete who narrowly missed qualifying for the Asian Games before an injury ended that path; he also heads the Goenka & Associates Educational Trust, running eight schools with 22,000+ students in Mumbai and Thane.
notes: Has a long legal history (2G spectrum case - acquitted 2017; other cases dropped/quashed 2025-26); avoid these topics in outreach. Company IR email is from the 2026 AGM notice.

name: Ajay Banga
current_role: President, World Bank Group (five-year term from June 2, 2023)
profile: Former President and CEO of Mastercard (2010-2021) and later Vice Chairman at General Atlantic, whose fortune comes largely from Mastercard equity. Since 2023 he has led the World Bank Group, pushing a jobs-first agenda, private-capital mobilisation (Private Sector Investment Lab) and Mission 300 to connect 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030.
interesting_fact: As World Bank president he championed the effort to connect 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030 - a direct energy-access hook for an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a Nestle India management trainee in 1981 (13 years there), then at PepsiCo helped launch Pizza Hut and KFC in India as the economy liberalised; during Citigroup training he briefly worked as a debt collector.

public_contacts.value: speakersbureau@worldbank.org (World Bank speakers bureau - for speaker requests)

notes: Highly public; best route for a podcast request is World Bank media relations or speakers bureau. Co-founder of the Cyber Readiness Institute; Padma Shri 2016; former ICC chairman.

name: David Thompson
current_role: Deceased (co-founder of Hillsdown Holdings; co-owner of Cheveley Park Stud, Newmarket; died 29 Dec 2020, aged 84)
profile: British businessman who co-founded food group Hillsdown Holdings and, with wife Patricia, bought Cheveley Park Stud in Newmarket in 1975, building one of Britain's leading racehorse breeding and ownership operations. Died 29 December 2020.
interesting_fact: He and his wife bought Cheveley Park, Newmarket's oldest stud farm, in 1975.
notes: Deceased - sources: https://thoroughbreddailynews.com/cheveley-park-studs-david-thompson-dies-at-84/ and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Thompson_(British_businessman). The SEC insider link (American Financial Group subsidiary president) is a different, unrelated David Thompson. Not a podcast candidate.

name: Jeffrey Soffer
profile: Son of Aventura, Florida developer Donald Soffer; ran family firm Turnberry Associates with sister Jackie for two decades before forming Fontainebleau Development in 2019. Owns the historic Fontainebleau Miami Beach (about $800m reinvested) and completed Fontainebleau Las Vegas, which opened in Dec 2023; also owns JW Marriott Turnberry and Big Easy Casino.
interesting_fact: Fontainebleau Las Vegas took nearly 20 years from land purchase to opening: Soffer halted it about three-quarters built after the 2008-09 crisis, then reacquired it in 2021 with Koch Real Estate Investments and finished it in late 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He calls philanthropy 'really personal' and focuses on cancer causes via the Bleau Cares platform (Susan G. Komen Miami, Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, Miami Dolphins Cancer Challenge); his career advice: 'Stay curious.'
notes: Does occasional interviews (Leaders magazine, Walker & Dunlop webcast). Avoid family/personal-life topics. Data-center/energy angle is weak; hospitality and mega-project development is the hook.

name: Li Liufa
current_role: Chairman/controlling shareholder, Tianrui Group (Henan) - steel casting, cement, tourism, minerals
profile: Henan entrepreneur who left a state fertilizer-factory job in 1985 to co-found a small farmer-owned steel casting plant in Ruzhou, then built Tianrui Group through takeovers of struggling cement plants and a state machinery works. Tianrui spans cement (HK-listed China Tianrui Group Cement), casting, cultural tourism and minerals; he handed day-to-day control of the cement arm to the next generation in 2022.
interesting_fact: In 1993 his small Ruzhou steel-casting works took over the state-owned Henan Yuxi Coal Mine Machinery Plant, a deal Chinese press called a 'snake swallowing an elephant'; he was twice ranked Henan's richest person by New Fortune (2011, 2012).
deep_cut_fact: After starting as a temporary worker at Linru County No. 2 Fertilizer Plant in 1975, he was recommended in 1980 to study Chinese literature at Henan University; his first plant made motor housings for combustion engines, reportedly taking ~70% of the national market.
notes: Low profile, Chinese-language media only. Tianrui Cement shares have been suspended and 2025 results delayed (2024 forced share sale) - avoid. Best route: company channels / HKEX filings.

name: Dani Reiss
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Canada Goose Holdings (NYSE/TSX: GOOS)
profile: Third-generation owner of Toronto outerwear brand Canada Goose, founded by his grandfather as Metro Sportswear in 1957. CEO since 2001, he repositioned it as a global luxury parka brand, took it public in 2017, keeps manufacturing in Canada, and in Sept 2026 bought additional shares, holding ~39% of multiple voting shares.
interesting_fact: In the early 2000s he walked down Toronto's Queen Street trying to get stores to carry his coats and every one said no; for years after taking over at 27 he avoided printing 'CEO' on his business cards.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the University of Toronto (BA 1997, Woodsworth College) in English literature and philosophy, wanted to travel and write short stories, and joined the family firm only to earn travel money for a few months.
notes: Media-friendly and gives many interviews (Fortune, U of T Magazine). Entrepreneurship/Made-in-Canada manufacturing is the natural hook. First business: flipping undervalued baseball cards in high school.
